q: How do I count remanufactured or refurbished parts I buy in Scope 3?
title: Remanufactured parts in Scope 3
short: Count them in Category 1, or Category 2 if you capitalise them, using the remanufacturer's own footprint for the part where you can get it. Otherwise estimate the remanufacturing energy plus the new components fitted. Do not use a new-part factor, which overstates them, and do not count them as zero.
audience: Fleet operators, OEM service networks and machinery users

p: Spare parts, reconditioned engines, gearboxes and pumps bought for maintenance are purchased goods, Category 1. A remanufactured machine or major assembly you record as a fixed asset goes in Category 2, capital goods, in the year you buy it, the same as a new one. The category follows how you account for the purchase, not whether the part is new.

sections.h: The order of data to use
ol: A product footprint from the remanufacturer for that part, cradle to its gate, ideally to ISO 14067.
Supplier-specific activity data: electricity and fuel used to strip, clean, machine and test the core, plus the footprint of new components fitted.
A spend-based estimate, labelled as such. Spend factors are built from new goods, so check whether a cheaper remanufactured part over or understates the result, and say so.

sections.h: What a remanufacturer footprint should cover
ul: Energy and consumables used in the remanufacturing plant.
New components that replace worn ones, such as bearings, seals and gaskets.
Transport of the old core to the plant, if the supplier arranges it.
It should not carry the emissions of making the original part; those belong to the first life.

sections.h: Do not net off the saving
p: The difference between a new part's footprint and a remanufactured one is an avoided emission. You may report it separately to show the benefit, but your Category 1 total should carry the remanufactured part's actual footprint, not the new-part figure minus a credit. If you pay to send old cores back, that freight is in Category 4.

example.title: Illustrative example: 40 remanufactured engines for a fleet
lines: Remanufacturing electricity reported by the supplier: 150 kWh per engine; x 0.710 (FY 2024-25 grid factor) = 106.5 kg CO2
New components fitted, from the supplier's footprint: 60 kg CO2e per engine (illustrative)
Fleet purchase: 166.5 x 40 = 6,660 kg, about 6.7 tonnes CO2e in Category 1
example.note: The component figure is CO2e because it covers several gases; the electricity part is CO2 only. Figures are illustrative; use the supplier's data.

senseible: Senseible keeps supplier invoices for these purchases in a separate supplier evidence trail, and where only spend is known it gives a spend-based estimate labelled with its wider uncertainty.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Technical Guidance for Calculating Scope 3 Emissions (2013), Categories 1 and 2
